questions.q: In the lesson's standard vesting shape, what happens to unlocked tokens during the cliff period?
options: Zero tokens unlock, regardless of the total vesting duration
Tokens unlock at double the normal rate
All tokens unlock immediately at the cliff's start
The cliff has no effect on unlocking
questions.explain: By definition, a cliff is an initial period during which zero tokens unlock, no matter how long the total vesting schedule runs.

questions.q: For a 4-year vesting schedule with a 1-year cliff and 2,400,000 total tokens, approximately how much is vested at month 24?
options: 2,400,000 tokens
0 tokens
800,000 tokens
1,200,000 tokens

questions.q: After the cliff ends in the worked example, what is the monthly token release rate?
options: 200,000 tokens/month
66,667 tokens/month
2,400,000 tokens/month
0 tokens/month
questions.explain: The remaining 36 months after the cliff release the full 2,400,000 tokens in equal increments: 2,400,000 / 36 = 66,667 tokens/month.

questions.q: Why does a cliff specifically help prevent early dumping, beyond what a long vesting duration alone would do?
options: A cliff has no additional effect beyond vesting duration
Cliffs only apply to governance tokens, not utility tokens
A cliff guarantees the token price will rise
Without a cliff, insiders could sell immediately after the token generation event, directly into launch-day demand
questions.explain: The cliff specifically blocks any unlocking in the earliest period, which is when insiders would otherwise be able to sell straight into the demand a launch creates.

questions.q: What does a long cliff and vesting duration signal to the market, per this lesson?
options: That the project has no real token utility
That the team plans to sell immediately once liquid
Confidence -- insiders are accepting illiquidity on the same (or stricter) terms they're asking public holders to accept risk under
Nothing -- vesting length has no signaling value
questions.explain: A long cliff/vesting schedule is a credible signal because insiders are locking themselves into the same long-term exposure they're asking the market to trust.
